label: the CRC register starts at zero, not at one
the CRC lands one bit early
the padding re-reads +0x118 instead of the register it was loaded into
why: PROVEN EQUIVALENT, and the proof is the interesting part.  The object loads +0x118 once into %edx before the pad loop, and that loop can reach index 0xfc, which IS +0x118 -- so `i < byte_118` re-reading the field would stop early and `i < len` would not.  It does not: `bits` is declared 0xe6 long, GCC uses that bound to conclude that `bits[i]` cannot alias the member at +0x118, and hoists the load out of the loop in BOTH forms.  Compiling the two with this tree's own CXXFLAGS and diffing `objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn` over the whole object gives one differing line, the file name in objdump's banner.  So the local copy in our source is legibility rather than necessity, and the mutation cannot be caught by any test -- which is why it is recorded here rather than left as an untested claim.  Finding 1386.

label: NOTE: the CRC pair landed with this batch
why: `calcCRC` (0x1f170) and `evaluateCRC` (0x1f470) put a THIRD and FOURTH copy of the shift register in this file -- the original's own repetition, not an inlining, for finding 1237's reason -- so every anchor below names the member it means.  The first five are the ONE trap this pair has: the V.90 CP twin bounds the information bits with `word_3bb0 - 0x11` and finds the peer's CRC at `word_3bb0 - 0x10`, and 0xbb-0x11 is 0xaa while 0x55-0x11 is 0x44, so a transcription of the CP source is indistinguishable from the MP source on every object the class itself can build.  t_v90mp.cpp's inconsistent type/+0x119 pairs are what tell them apart, and these mutations are what prove those trials work.
